subject: Orpheus Health — IR notification windows, BCP/DR artifacts, and vendor questionnaire
summary: Post-demo security follow-up covering IR notification windows, required BCP/DR evidence, and next steps to complete the vendor questionnaire.

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.inference.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@orpheushealth.com>
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.inference.com, neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Orpheus Health — IR notification windows, BCP/DR artifacts, and vendor questionnaire

Hi Alicia — thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and the security items you asked us to surface so your InfoSec/legal teams can move forward: 

- Incident notification windows: Redwood's standard is initial customer notification within 24 hours of confirmed detection of an incident that impacts customer data availability or confidentiality; we follow-up with a detailed incident report within 72 hours for GDPR-relevant incidents and provide a forensic timeline within 14 days when applicable. For HIPAA-covered data, we work with customers on the 60-day breach reporting cadence and will provide all required evidence for their HIPAA notification process.

- BCP/DR artifacts: attached is a high-level BCP summary (redwood_bcp_summary.pdf) that includes RTO/RPO targets for Dedicated and Private deployments, backup cadence, cross-region failover steps, and test frequency. We can provide additional logs and runbook exports scoped to your environment once a contract/connection is established.

- SOC 2: we run on a SOC 2 Type II control set; recent report attached (soc2-type2-report-redwood-2025.pdf). If you need a bridge letter or an SSAE attestation excerpt for specific controls, let us know the control IDs and we'll extract relevant artifacts.

- Vendor questionnaire: I attached the vendor questionnaire you shared in the meeting (orpheus_vendor_q.xlsx). Neha will start filling the technical controls and will tag anything that requires legal review or a policy excerpt.

Next steps I propose: 
1) Neha to return the completed technical tab by end of Monday (Apr 13).
2) Ben to schedule a 30-min call with your security team to walk through any answers that need context (suggest Wed Apr 15).
3) If helpful, we can open a secure share folder for artifacts and a limited-access view into our incident runbook excerpts.

Can you confirm the right contacts (legal@orpheushealth.com + Tom Hwang for engineering) and whether any of the timelines above need to be shortened?

Thanks — Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Hi Evelyn — really appreciate the quick follow-up and the attachments. A couple of clarifications from our side: 

- Notification SLA expectations: our legal team prefers an initial notification within 12 hours for incidents that expose PHI or PII. Is Redwood able to commit to a 12-hour initial notice for HIPAA-impacting events?

- For the detailed incident report, can you confirm whether the 72-hour deliverable includes: timeline of detection, scope of affected customers, root cause hypothesis, and immediate mitigation steps? We want to ensure it aligns with our internal playbook.

- The vendor questionnaire: Tom will own most of the engineering/ops checks; legal will take policy and contract questions. We sent an extra worksheet to the file (you should see a tab named ORPHEUS-LEGAL) that needs a few policy excerpts and a copy of your encryption-at-rest key management spec.

Please let me know if the 12-hour initial notice is possible and whether Neha can also provide a short note on key rotation cadence and KMS integrations. Thanks — Alicia

--
Alicia Gomez
Director, Information Security | Orpheus Health
alicia.gomez@orpheushealth.com
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com>

Date: Sun, 12 Apr 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Orpheus Health — IR notification windows, BCP/DR artifacts, and vendor questionnaire

Hi Alicia — thanks, copied answers below inline and marked items that will need artifact pulls or legal review. I filled the ORPHEUS-LEGAL tab where appropriate and added comments in the vendor worksheet (changes tracked).

- 12-hour initial notification: Operationally we can support an expedited initial notification for confirmed incidents that impact PHI/PII. Two caveats: (1) "confirmed" means our detection/triage has established a credible incident affecting customer data; we will send an interim alert within 12 hours and follow with a more detailed update as we validate scope. (2) For advanced forensic time-to-confirm we may need brief coordination with your team to avoid contaminating evidence.

- 72-hour report contents: yes — the 72-hour report includes detection timeline, affected scope (to the best of our knowledge at that time), mitigation actions taken, and a root-cause hypothesis. The 72-hour deliverable is intended as an initial formal report; deeper forensics and final RCA will follow (typically within 14–30 days depending on complexity).

- KMS/key rotation: we integrate with customer-managed KMS for Private deployments and support Redwood-managed KMS for Hosted with quarterly key rotation by default; rotation cadence can be changed to monthly on request. Encryption keys are AES-256 for at-rest and TLS 1.3 for all in-transit links. We added a short artifact note in the ORPHEUS-LEGAL tab pointing to the KMS integration guide. (Artifact: kms-integration.md — available on secure share once you confirm accounts.)

- BCP/DR specifics: RTO targets: 15 minutes for control-plane failover (multi-tenant Hosted), 1–4 hours for Dedicated capacity depending on config, and sub-6-hour for Private deployments when cross-region failover is configured. RPO: generally 1 hour for model state (KV cache snapshot cadence) and 24 hours for backup snapshots; we can increase snapshot frequency for Dedicated contracts.

Attachments included in this message: a filled technical worksheet extract (attachment stub: orpheus_vendor_q_filled_tech.xlsx). Items requiring legal review: encryption key management specs, SOC 2 exception notes (if any), and our standard DPA snippet for breach notification windows.

Let me know if you want Neha to walk Tom through the technical rows on Wed; I can block 30 minutes.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Security Architect | Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.inference.com
